OWNER ANSWER: alternative A. Generated captions cannot license film SurfaceExplicit. Asked and answered in the Claude Code session of 21 September 2026; the question carried the concrete trigger ("John opens the door", parsed and accepted with exact film support) and both disclosed alternatives from the brief committed at e52f62f6 (docs/refactor/evidence/d1a-film-phase-plan-20260920/owner-decision-brief.md, SHA-256 13a03b010b5abf427d3c12bb7eacb001e21d4276ba19140746fac5a35516d530), which links F4.

Record: docs/refactor/evidence/film-f0-claim-status-20260921/README.md at 473c69593d16e378d03fad7f4e55a16145bb8c53, with the constructor/join/provenance/component/consistency/StatusWeight consequences. Also a dated decision note in ADR 0007 and PLAN.md section 6. Consequences in brief: SurfaceExplicit keeps its text meaning; ClaimMeta span law unchanged; caption-only film claims are Hypothesized with complete derivation (fallback StatusWeight 0.25; calibrated credence overrides, raw score does not); HumanAdjudicated needs a claim-specific adjudication record; no license basis, component version or wire change; text overlap/causal-cue rules declared inapplicable to film inputs; F4 supplies an explicit per-family rule rather than reusing text SurfaceExplicit assignments. F4 must cite this record. Nothing implemented; no build required.
